items.t: Rusted steel brake lines can burst
items.job: Replace corroded brake lines and bleed brakes
items.note: Price assumes a full set of lines along the frame. Fixing one short section costs less.

items.t: Dashboard gauges stick or read wrong
items.job: Remove cluster and replace gauge stepper motors
items.note: A mail-in cluster rebuild service is a common lower-cost option.
Rusty tank straps or lines can add time.

items.t: Knock sensor codes on the V8
items.job: Replace both knock sensors, harness and intake gaskets
items.note: The intake manifold must come off, so sensors and harness are done together.

items.t: Blower motor resistor fails or burns its connector
items.job: Replace blower motor resistor and connector
items.note: If the blower motor itself is worn, replacing it too costs more.

items.t: Front wheel speed sensor and hub failure
items.job: Replace front wheel hub bearing assembly
items.note: Price is per side. The ABS sensor is built into the hub on most of these trucks.
If only the dash 4WD switch is bad, the repair costs less.

items.t: Clunk in the steering at low speed
items.note: Sometimes a lube service on the shaft stops the clunk for less.
A used unit costs less. A local rebuild is also common and may cost less.

items.job: Replace pistons and rings and AFM oil shield
items.note: Some trucks are helped first by a cheaper valve cover or oil shield fix; ask the dealer.

items.job: Replace lifters, camshaft and lifter guides
items.note: Cost rises a lot if the engine must be replaced. Some trucks have a lifter warranty; ask the dealer.

items.t: Loss of brake assist from vacuum pump
items.note: Usually free under the recall. Check your VIN or ask a GMC dealer.

items.job: Flush transmission with updated fluid per GM bulletin
items.note: If the torque converter is damaged, replacing it costs much more.
Usually free under the recall. Check your VIN or ask a GMC dealer.
Covered under the recall if the VIN qualifies; some engines only need inspection and an oil change. Ask the dealer.
